title: Canonical completed-ring strict open exchange
statement: For an adic datum $(A,I)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and an open Cartesian square $s$ as in [def-cbc-open-immersion-square], write $E_j$ for sheafified module extension, constructed from [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] and [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], over the actual completed rings $A_T$. Define $J_j$ by applying $E_j$ at every strict tower index and deriving this exact functor, and likewise for $j'$. Let $G_g,G_{g_U}$ be the total derived levelwise module pullbacks of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Define the simultaneous inverse strict diagram map by applying the ordinary completed-ring inverse open exchange at every index, with its ordinary sectionwise Cartesian right-adjoint normalization. Define $\beta:G_g\circ J_j\simeq J_{j'}\circ G_{g_U}$ as the unique derived natural isomorphism characterized on every objectwise K-flat strict tower complex $P$ by the equation: $\beta^{-1}_{QP}$ followed by the source model map equals the target model map followed by the image of the strict inverse map under localization. Here $\gamma$ is that fixed simultaneous inverse strict map, and the two model maps are the composites of the exact-extension factor and the actual universal pullback counit, in the indicated source and target orders. On reduction towers define the reduced exchange by precomposition with the actual completed reduction functor. No completed ring-map invertibility, quasi-compactness, completeness, constructibility or boundedness is imposed.

proof.text: Whiskering the existing additive exact open extension with the tower index preserves additivity, finite limits and finite colimits, since diagram limits and colimits are computed at every index.

Apply naturality of the fixed ordinary inverse exchange to each tower transition and to each component of a tower morphism. These assemble its simultaneous strict lift. Its components are isomorphisms, so the strict natural transformation is invertible.

Apply a single functorial reduced flat resolution to the strict diagram of cochain complexes, and transpose back to a cochain complex of towers. Prove the flatness and K-flatness of the resolution with the monoidal category and its reduced resolution abstract. Each evaluated tower complex is explicitly isomorphic to its resolved component, so K-flatness transports without unfolding the total tensor. Functoriality preserves all transitions, and evaluation detects the augmentation quasi-isomorphism.

Take the recorded completed pullback functors with their actual universal counits as the derived models. Completed open extension preserves the smaller flat-term K-flat resolving class by the completed open K-flat lemma. Apply the existing normalized model-pull descent theorem through a private generic helper accepting the derived pairs directly. Invert the resulting isomorphism; its complex-counit equation is exactly the stated HEq normalization, and uniqueness follows by inversion. The normalization definition specializes a generic representative predicate with exactly the original displayed equation. Matching this named predicate avoids expansion of the concrete completed pullbacks during kernel checking. The ordinary-model descent proof remains in this module.
